newsitem.title: CHINA: China insurer pays out $400 mln for flood losses.
newsitem.headline: China insurer pays out $400 mln for flood losses.

text.p: The People's Insurance Company of China Group (PICC) has paid 3.312 billion yuan ($399 million) to cover losses caused during three months of flooding from June to August, the Economic Daily said on Wednesday.
The official newspaper did not say what proportion of claims stemmed from damage from the raging floods that scourged swathes of central and southern China this summer.
Estimates in July of flood-related losses hit 94.1 billion yuan in the worst-hit provinces of Anhui, Guizhou, Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Guangxi and Sichuan.

Tens of thousands of PICC staff were "fighting on the front line of investigation and assessment" to ensure all claims were settled by November, the newspaper quoted PICC general manager Ma Yongwei as saying.

The group had sent out more than 2,000 groups to help flood victims and assess claims, and had broken common practice by establishing a 24 hour service. Branches were already settling up to 92 percent of claims within a month, it said.
PICC had donated money and goods worth more than 20 million yuan, it said without elaborating.
The state-owned PICC insurance group dominates the Chinese market, taking around 79 percent of all premiums.
